mechanism: Both drugs have anticholinergic and CNS depressant properties; disulfiram may inhibit metabolism of oxybutynin through CYP3A4 inhibition, increasing oxybutynin levels and anticholinergic effects.
action: Monitor for increased anticholinergic adverse effects (dry mouth, urinary retention, constipation, confusion); consider dose reduction of oxybutynin or alternative antimuscarinic agent if CNS effects develop.
